summary: Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and sinologist who earned his bachelor's from the University of British Columbia, an MA from National Taiwan University, and a PhD from SOAS under D. C. Lau. He served at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1978–2016).

Roland Barthes worked in philosophy and linguistics, studying at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, Lycée Montaigne, and the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the CNRS (~1952–1959), EHESS (~1962–1976), and the Collège de France (1976–1980).

Roland Ferenczi is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. His academic posts (both attested 2026) include visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University and project staff member at the University of Hamburg.
Roland Steiner is a scholar in Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn (attested 1990). He held an assistant professorship at the University of Marburg (attested 2002).

Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who earned his doctorate from the University of Salzburg (2002) and completed his habilitation at Heidelberg University. He held posts at ZMO, Humboldt University, Heidelberg University (2008, 2014), Basel (2013–2014), and Munich (2017).

Rolf Alfred Stein worked in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, studying at SOS, INALCO, and EPHE under Pelliot, Maspero, Chavannes, and Bacot, among others. He was directeur d'études at EPHE (1951–1975) and professor at the Collège de France (1965–1982).
Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Helmut Tauscher (attested 2010).

Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University and completed her doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. She held professorships at the University of Delhi (1963–1970) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (1970–1991; Chair 1993).
Ron Garry is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer was an author and psychiatrist active in Buddhist studies. He studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and with the traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a sociologist specializing in Tibetology. He has served as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland (attested 1998) and as an Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and management, having studied under traditional teacher Koshin Ogui in 1985. He held an associate professorship at Loyola University Chicago (~1989–1995) and became a management professor at San Francisco State University (~1995).

Ronald Egan is a Sinologist who earned his PhD from Harvard University (~1970–1977). He held appointments at Harvard (~1977–1983), Wellesley College (~1983–1987), UC Santa Barbara (~1987–2012; emeritus ~2012), and Stanford University (~2012–2023).

Ronald Eric Emmerick specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Oxford (~1961–1964) under Harold Walter Bailey and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg (1971–2001).

Ronald Inden is a scholar of Indology and history. He held a long-term academic post at the University of Chicago, serving as Professor Emeritus of History and South Asian Languages and Civilizations (attested 2007, 2026).

Ronald M. Davidson works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at UC Berkeley (-1985) studying under Lancaster, Jaini, Strickmann, and Staal, among others, and held an academic post at Fairfield University (attested 2002–2005).

Ronald Neufeldt is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He spent his academic career at the University of Calgary (~1974–2006), serving as associate professor (~1980–1990) and later becoming Professor Emeritus (~2006).

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1974–1980). He held positions at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (assistant professor ~1987) and Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).
Rong Geng was a Chinese scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and linguistics. He studied at Peking University (~1922–1925) and subsequently held a post at Yenching University (~1926–1941).

Rongdao Lai works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She received her PhD from McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates (attested 2013) and was appointed assistant professor there (attested 2026).
